- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.4 step 4 "Read failure (exit-2 equivalent) → no renew"
  PROBLEM: A single transient `check_pr_hand_back` read failure (exit 2) causes the script to skip `renew` for every subscriber in the repo, so every enabled hand-back Routine fires within ≤90 min in its bound session.
  WHY: §26.C step 3 today tolerates a read failure for 7 days before the dead-man's switch fires; the plan compresses that to 90 min with no per-PR retry/backoff. A bursty but recoverable read error would falsely page every pushing session.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.3 step 4 "set_session_title … only when k, h, f, b or e changed since the title's numbers"
  PROBLEM: The plan only renames the session when one of the integer counters changes, so the embedded `<HH:MM> UTC` timestamp in the title can go stale by up to an hour even though a tick ran.
  WHY: This is observability, not correctness — but the stated goal is that "the master's title records its last tick" (Risks), and the chosen guard defeats that when nothing changes.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.1 row "Master-mode hand-back Routine" and A.4 step 2 "legacy Routines are skipped"
  PROBLEM: The plan claims the prefix `CLAUDE.md §26 hand-back for PR #<n> (<PR URL>).` is byte-identical to today's so `stale_routines.py`'s `HAND_BACK_PROMPT_PATTERN` still matches, but does not assert the same for `ROLE_PROMPT_PATTERN` / `VIA_PROMPT_PATTERN` (the new tokens) and does not document how `stale_routines.classify` distinguishes a "PR #<n> hand-back" Routine whose new tokens are present from one whose new tokens are absent but whose name still matches the legacy prefix.
  WHY: Today, every hand-back Routine ends with `. Continue with CLAUDE.md §26.D in this session.` The new prompt inserts `Role: … Via: master. Fallback next steps: …` between the URL and that suffix. If `stale_routines.py` matches by suffix string, it still works; if it ever moves to substring matching for the suffix (or `Fallback next steps:` is treated as part of the suffix and the user's text contains another "Continue with CLAUDE.md §26.D" fragment), the sweeper can misclassify master Routines. A misclassification could delete an enabled master hand-back or skip a stale sent marker.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.5 step 2 "A session only creates a master when its own depth, found by walking `parent_session_id` with `get_session` (at most 8 calls, the pickup's method), is ≤3"
  PROBLEM: The depth walk uses `get_session` and is capped at "at most 8 calls" but the plan never specifies a stop condition when a `parent_session_id` chain contains a non-numeric, archived, or self-referential entry.
  WHY: The plan describes the depth check in prose only — there is no error path for a broken chain, no early-exit when `parent_session_id` is missing or equal to the current id, and no limit on how many calls the master itself spends before concluding. On a malformed chain the master either times out or reports "depth unknown" and falls back to the pickup, increasing the worst-case revival latency.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.4 step 4 (terminal `sent` marker → `fallback_notify` + `fb` suffix) and Tests section P-5 probe
  PROBLEM: The plan's dedup for terminal `fallback_notify` relies on renaming an ended (fired) Routine to `… sent <state> <sha7> fb` via `update_trigger`. But the `sent` marker is a `run_once_at` Routine that has already fired and is in the ended/completed state. Probe P-5 only tests `update_trigger` with `name` on Routines created by another session and on recurring Routines — it does NOT test `update_trigger` on ended/fired Routines. If the claude.ai API refuses `update_trigger` on an ended Routine, the `fb` suffix cannot be applied, and the master would emit `fallback_notify` (with a PushNotification) on every subsequent tick until the 6h stale sweep deletes the marker — up to 6 duplicate notifications over 6 hours.
  WHY: The plan's Risks section acknowledges renaming might fail ("If only renaming fails, the design cannot store dedup outside the conversation, and the flip does not ship"), but P-5 as specified would not catch this because it doesn't test the ended-Routine case that the `fb` suffix actually needs.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.5 step 2 — "then a one-shot `PR status master: <owner>/<repo> first tick` trigger 2 min out"
  PROBLEM: The first-tick trigger name `PR status master: <owner>/<repo> first tick` exceeds the 60-char Routine name cap for the longest consumer. For `shubhodeep1/drhyg_ecommerce_automation` the name is 67 chars (`PR status master: ` = 18, repo = 38, ` first tick` = 11). The plan correctly accounts for the 60-char cap on the recurring tick Routine name (A.1: "≤60 chars; the longest consumer … gives 56") but does not account for it on the first-tick trigger name. The truncated name (`… f…`) is cosmetically unfortunate but not functionally broken — the master matches on the recurring cron Routine name, not the first-tick trigger name, and `is_ours` would still match the truncated name via the `PR status master: ` prefix.
  WHY: No runtime failure — the first-tick trigger fires correctly regardless of name truncation; the name is for human readability only. The `stale_routines.py` sweep would still match and clean it up via the `PR status master: ` prefix.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- docs/plans/stateless-pr-status-master-checker-plan.md:A.4 step 4 — "call `check_pr_hand_back` once"; A.4 intro — "imports `check_pr_hand_back` and `read_fix_claims` from `check_in_status.py`"
  PROBLEM: The plan does not specify what `stuck_hours` and `min_age_hours` values to pass to `check_pr_hand_back(repo, number, stuck_hours, min_age_hours, now, ignore_claim_by)`.
  WHY: The per-PR checker (§26.C step 1) passes `DEFAULT_STUCK_HOURS=6.0` and `min_age_hours=0.0`; the sweep (`claude_pr_sweep.py`) passes `min_age_hours=2.0` (`CLAUDE_PR_SWEEP_MIN_AGE_HOURS`). If the implementer picks `min_age_hours=2.0`, due fixes would be delayed by 2 hours versus today's per-PR checker behavior. If `stuck_hours` is omitted, `claude/implement-plan-*` heads would not get their 6-hour stuck window. The plan should specify these values explicitly (likely `stuck_hours=DEFAULT_STUCK_HOURS`, `min_age_hours=0.0` to match the per-PR checker the master replaces).
  WHY: The master would either delay fixes (with `min_age_hours=2.0`) or miss the implement-plan stuck window (with `stuck_hours=0`), depending on the implementer's choice.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
